subject: PeregrinePay: Dedicated pool throughput ceiling — request for prioritized fallback, burst credits, and exec alignment
messages:
From: Peregrine Pay <ops@peregrinepay.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Persistent request queueing & 5xxs on dedicated pool (PeregrinePay)

Hi Redwood support,

We've been seeing a sustained increase in token latency and periodic 5xx responses on our dedicated pool since 08:45 PDT this morning. Request queues are growing and throughput on our reserved capacity is about 35% under contractual expectation for the 09:00–11:30 window (we run a steady inference workload for real-time scoring). This is causing retries and downstream customer-facing errors.

We attached a short log sample and a token-per-second snapshot. Can you confirm whether this is a localized pool saturation or something on your routing layer? We need immediate mitigation and an ask: provisional burst credits and confirmation of fallback routes (hosted model or lower-capacity model) while you investigate.

Please escalate if necessary — our CEO is monitoring.

Thanks,
Marta Ortega
CFO, Peregrine Pay
ops@peregrinepay.com

Attachments: peregrine_ops_logs_jun4.txt (text), throughput_snapshot_0900-1200.csv (csv)

From: logan_wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, david_kim <david@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Persistent request queueing & 5xxs on dedicated pool (PeregrinePay)

Folks — forwarding Peregrine's ops note. They report sustained under-delivery vs reserved throughput and customer-visible 5xx spikes. Marked as high-priority; Marta copied the CFO/CEO. Immediate asks: 1) confirm if dedicated GPU pool host-level saturation or routing fallbacks failing, 2) whether we can temporarily enable burst capacity for them and 3) propose a fallback path (hosted smaller model or pre-warmed fallback) we can activate within 30 minutes.

Marissa, David — can you triage the pool (logs, host metrics, kv-cache health) and call out any noisy neighbor or auto-scale failures? Priyom — if we need a policy exception for provisional burst credits, can you advise on fast-approval path and how much we can authorize before leadership approval? Irene — please prepare a one-slide status for an exec sync if we need to escalate.

-- Logan
Principal Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: david_kim <david@redwood.com>
To: logan_wright <logan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Persistent request queueing & 5xxs on dedicated pool (PeregrinePay)

On Fri, Jun 4, 2027 at 09:22 Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding Peregrine's ops note.

Quick triage: the dedicated pool serving Peregrine (ded-pool-58, us-west-2a) shows elevated GPU utilization and sustained host-side queueing. There's a high rate of long-running requests from a single client token pattern — appears to be a large batch of long-context scoring jobs that started around 08:40. KV-cache hit rate dropped (60% -> 18%) which explains token-level regen. I don't see cross-region routing issues — traffic is landing on the correct pool.

Immediate remediation steps taken (already in-progress):
- Enabled emergency soft-throttle for heavy request class to reduce head-of-line blocking (5 min window)
- Increased eviction aggressiveness on prefix cache for that client
- Spun up two temporary hosts in the same pool and started warming them with the model; new hosts show healthy readiness but we need ~8–12 minutes to fully reach steady-state for long-context requests.

For customer-facing mitigation: we can redirect low-priority scoring to the hosted fallback (model:redwood-small-v2) with minimal change, and keep high-priority traffic on the reserved pool. That will reduce reserve throughput pressure by ~25% estimated.

I'll stay on the bridge. If burst credits are needed to cover the extra hosts, Priyom — please advise policy.

— David
Sr. Tech Ops, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: logan_wright <logan@redwood.com>, david_kim <david@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Persistent request queueing & 5xxs on dedicated pool (PeregrinePay)

On Fri, Jun 4, 2027 at 09:38 David Kim <david@redwood.com> wrote:
> Immediate remediation steps taken (already in-progress):

We can approve a provisional burst credit to cover the two temp hosts for up to 4 hours immediately (policy: up to $X approved by SE manager). For anything beyond that, we need an expedited leadership exception. I'm authorizing an initial 4-hour buffer; finance will reconcile and we can convert to formal credit if root cause traces to our scheduling/oversubscription.

Operational notes for activation:
- Logan/Marissa: we need customer authorization to switch lower-priority traffic to hosted fallback (we should propose a scoped agreement to avoid surprises).
- David: please push a communication to Peregrine with the short plan and ETA for full remediation.

I'll stand by to escalate to Marcus/CM if leadership approval is required beyond the 4-hour window.

— Priyom
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: logan_wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Peregrine Pay <ops@peregrinepay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Persistent request queueing & 5xxs on dedicated pool (PeregrinePay)

Hi Marta — quick update from the team and proposed short-term plan:

1) What happened: one large workload pattern initiated long-context scoring at ~08:40 which reduced KV cache effectiveness and drove host queues up on your dedicated pool (ded-pool-58). Hosts showed GPU saturation leading to transient 5xx errors for queue-front requests.

2) Immediate mitigations (already executed):
- David enabled soft-throttles and warmed two extra hosts (these will be fully warmed by ~16:40 PDT).
- We can route lower-priority scoring to hosted fallback model (redwood-small-v2) to recover ~25% throughput immediately; this requires your sign-off to activate routing on your tenant for up to 4 hours.
- Priyom authorized provisional burst credits to cover added host costs for 4 hours; Redwood will absorb this cost if we confirm the incident was caused by our scheduling/overcommit.

3) Asks / next steps:
- Please reply "approve fallback" if you want us to activate the hosted fallback routing now.
- If you prefer we attempt alternate per-tenant throttling only, say so and we'll keep all traffic on the dedicated pool while we continue the warm-up.
- We'll schedule a post-mortem and provide a remediation plan (model sharding suggestion, KV cache tuning, and a pre-warm policy) by EOD tomorrow.

We appreciate the urgency and we'll keep the channel open. If you'd like an exec bridge, say the word and we'll loop Marcus/CM.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Principal Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
